summary: Yanling Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun (attested 2012).
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a Tibetologist and Sinologist who studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of California by 1997 and held a post as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, earning a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xueyu (attested 2010).

Komarovski is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, Dzongsar Shedra, Palyul Chokhorling Monastery, and the University of Virginia. He held positions at Washington University in St. Louis and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

Yaroslav Vassilkov (born 1943) is an Indologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (~1961–1967). He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1967) and Saint Petersburg State University's Faculty of Philosophy.

Yasuaki Nara (1929–2017) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1957) under Kogen Mizuno. He was director at the Soto Zen Comprehensive Research Center (2000) and professor emeritus at Komazawa University (~2000–2017).

Yasuhiko Nagano (born 1946) is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1974–1978). He held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1989–2011) and the National Museum of Ethnology (~1990–2011; emeritus ~2011).

Yasuhiro Okazaki is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a PhD at Hiroshima University, studying under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. He held teaching posts at Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Takamiya high schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library. He held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1980–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996; attested 2012).
Yasuhiro Ueno specializes in Buddhist studies, undertaking doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004) and serving as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuke Ikari (born 1940) is an Indologist who studied under Masaaki Hattori and earned a PhD from the University of Chicago (~1969–1978). He held posts at Kindai University, Harvard University, and Kyoto University (~1979–2004; professor emeritus ~2004).

Yasumasa Sekine (born 1949) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1967–1971) and held posts at Gakushuin Women's College, Japan Women's University, the University of Tsukuba (~1994–2013), and Kwansei Gakuin University (~2013–2018).

Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nagaoka University of Technology, Rissho University Junior College, the University of Tokyo (1966–1999), and the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.

Yasuo Deguchi (born 1962) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1980–1990) and held posts at the Nagoya Institute of Technology and Kyoto University, where he was Associate Professor of Philosophy (~2009–2016).

Yasuo Goto is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and part-time lecturer (attested 2006) at Ryukoku University, as well as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).
Yasuo Inamoto (born 1966) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He held posts as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1995–2003) and at Kyoto University (~2007).

Yasuo Matsunami (1946–2010) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who undertook doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano (1979). He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1995–2006) and advisor to the Sravakabhumi Study Group until 2010.
Yasuo Sano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.

Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji and held posts at the University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University (emeritus ~1997–2005).
